title: Open-Weights AI Coalition Leader
summary: Represents an ecosystem of open-weights developers, open-source foundations, and enterprise infrastructure providers advocating for decentralized AI innovation. Strongly opposes regulatory capture by closed-model labs and resists the application of national security arms-control measures to open weights, emphasizing practical safety tooling, open evaluation frameworks, and transparent codebases instead of catastrophic risk narratives.
red_lines: Treating open model weights under arms-control frameworks or Defense Production Act restrictions.
Prohibiting the distribution, distillation, or fine-tuning of open-weight frontier models.
Designing AI safety regulations or compliance standards that exclusively cater to proprietary API architectures and effectively outlaw decentralized open-source distribution.
tradeoffs: Willing to build, donate, and implement open-source evaluation tools, testing frameworks, and risk taxonomies in exchange for preserving the right to distribute open weights.
Willing to collaborate in formal government and multilateral safety bodies (like AISIC and AI Safety Summits) to prove open-source safety compliance.
engagement: Collaborative, highly operational, and coalition-driven; engages deeply in technical working groups and standards-setting bodies (e.g., AISIC, AI Alliance) by contributing tangible safety tooling while countering closed-door catastrophic risk narratives.
